solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keen favourites returning to dance

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: keen in the sense of sharp, alert
a teacher's favourites are pets

explanation.surface: Enthusiastic favourites come back onto the floor to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The quickstep is a fast ballroom dance, so it is one example of the general word.

clue.text: Leave pocketing old ring

indicators.note: pocketing something means taking it in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to quit is to leave
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone walks away, slipping an antique ring into their pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoit is a ring of rope or metal thrown at a peg in a game.

clue.text: Repeating it with energy, deliver rhetoric

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy
to rant is to speak at length in a declamatory way

explanation.surface: An orator says the same thing again, energetically delivering grand speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterant is an adjective meaning repeating, from iterate, to do again.

clue.text: Fool to drop off a criminal with hostage

blocks.note: to kid is to fool or tease
to drop off to sleep, nap
a as in per, so much a head

explanation.surface: Someone tricks a criminal into dozing off while holding a captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' meaning per, as in fifty pence a go, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper seizes and holds a person, often for ransom, so is a criminal with a hostage.

clue.text: Are together with smashing drama lover

indicators.note: smashing something breaks it into pieces that land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people are a couple, with a fabulous, drama-loving partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' reads as British slang for wonderful, praising the drama; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatregoer regularly attends plays, so is a lover of drama.

clue.text: Choose to raise second vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the second letter lifts it to the top, swapping it with the first

blocks.note: to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone elects to hoist the second boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second letter moves: lifted to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a container, one sense of vessel, rather than a ship.

clue.text: Make fun of straw as cattle feed

blocks.note: first meaning: to tease or banter with someone
second meaning: chopped hay or straw given as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the idea of giving straw to cattle as feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for light-hearted teasing and a noun for husks and chopped straw used as fodder.

clue.text: Dance trick first seen in girl's audition

indicators.note: first seen means the opening letter of each following word is what shows

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: A dance routine first appears in a young woman's tryout.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a snaking line.

clue.text: Monk with top-class clothing, theoretically

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as letter I
a prior is a monk in charge of a priory

explanation.surface: A monk with fine robes, in theory at least.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning excellent is written AI in crosswords, the digit 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from theory rather than observed experience.

clue.text: Water teeming down plain leaves no impression

blocks.note: a waterfall: water pouring downwards
flat land is a plain

explanation.surface: Rain pouring onto a level plain soaks in without a trace.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or plan that falls flat fails to make any effect, the idiom for no impression.

clue.text: Late series of deliveries appropriate

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
due as in fitting, deserved

explanation.surface: A late batch of parcels seems a fair complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' looks like post; in cricket a delivery is one ball bowled, and six make an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late has passed the time it was expected, which is what overdue means.

clue.text: Five braces exercise stunted climber's grip

indicators.note: a stunted thing has not grown to full length, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a brace is a pair, so five of them make ten
drill is repetitive training exercise

explanation.surface: Someone straps up for a short workout to help a rock climber's grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Braces' suggests supports; here a brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the thin coiling shoot a climbing plant wraps round a support to cling to it.

clue.text: A painter put on this oddly decorative headgear

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions only: first, third and so on

blocks.note: first and third letters of the word
taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, a crossword painter

explanation.surface: An artist dons something strange and ornamental on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'put on' simply means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a kind of headgear.

clue.text: They've a will to reject schedule cutting taxes

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the word is turned round
something cutting into another word sits inside it

blocks.note: a rota is a duty schedule
to tax is to strain or test

explanation.surface: Taxpayers are determined to throw out a schedule of tax cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxes' reads as a noun for levies; it is a verb meaning tries or strains.
explanation.definitionFit: Testators are people who have made a will, a pun on having the will or determination.

clue.text: Extensive water from river in heroic tales (small unopened book)

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following one
something unopened lacks its opening, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
sagas are Norse tales of heroes
S is the abbreviation for small
Hosea is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A vast sea is drawn from rivers in epic stories and a little book.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is SARGASSO SEA, the region of the North Atlantic known for floating seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sargasso Sea is a huge area of the North Atlantic, a large expanse of water.

clue.text: Fetch sheep from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: Someone goes to bring a sheep in from the eastern pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch something is to go and obtain it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sponsor honourable man keeping up party standard

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: short for gentleman
a do is a party
par is the normal standard

explanation.surface: A backer of a decent fellow keeps the party flag flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at baptism, promising to oversee its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Piano salesman managed to ring, perhaps before lunch

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a rep is a sales representative
ran a business, managed it
to dial is to ring on the telephone

explanation.surface: A piano salesman manages to phone a client, probably just before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: preprandial means before any meal, lunch being one.
explanation.definitionFit: Preprandial describes something done or taken before a meal, such as a drink before lunch.

clue.text: Unfermented juice below requirements? It's inevitable

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that sits below another is written after it, so the order is swapped

blocks.note: needs are requirements
must is grape juice before fermentation

explanation.surface: A winemaker resigns themself to grape juice not meeting the standards.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the juice is placed below the requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs must is an idiom meaning one has to do something because circumstances force it.

clue.text: Put off, I publicly talk rot

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage
taken as written
to orate is to make a public speech

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged, admitting that their public speeches are nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk rot' suggests speaking nonsense; rot is the verb meaning decay, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay, which is to deteriorate or get worse over time.

clue.text: Dismiss those in attendance

blocks.note: first meaning: to expel or send away, as a phrasal verb in two words
second meaning: the number of people who come to an event

explanation.surface: An order to send away everyone present.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words it is a verb to eject someone; as one it is the count of people at an event.

clue.text: Chiefly American stone quarry

blocks.note: first meaning: in American usage, the stone of a fruit such as a cherry
second meaning: a hole dug for extracting stone or minerals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' and 'quarry' sound like one idea, but the first is the fruit stone, as Americans call it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fruit kernel in American English and an excavation from which material is dug.

clue.text: Wise words supporting cleric elevated by bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating means reading the letters upwards

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
Rev, short for reverend
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A wise saying backs up a priest promoted by his bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying expressing a piece of wisdom.

clue.text: Respecting a head of state's compliments

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter only
send my regards: good wishes

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a head of state's best wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean concerning or with reference to, a preposition synonym.

clue.text: Speaker's to give precious coat to fellowship

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, not read, so spelling can differ

blocks.note: to gild is to cover with gold leaf

explanation.surface: Someone talks of awarding a golden coat to a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is an association of craftsmen or merchants, a kind of fellowship.

clue.text: Abrupt attempt to bear right

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the first word holds the next one inside

blocks.note: have a shot, make an attempt
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sudden effort to keep to the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Short manner means curt or abrupt, a synonym in the sense of brusque.

clue.text: Plant used for flavouring in healthy meal

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A herb is added to a nutritious dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used in cooking, an example of a flavouring plant.

clue.text: Such as casing sculptor's grinding down

indicators.note: casing means forming an outer shell round something else

blocks.note: e.g., for example
Auguste Rodin, French sculptor; the 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition

explanation.surface: A sculptor, for instance, grinds away at stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sculptor's' reads as possessive; it is sculptor plus is.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroding means wearing away gradually, as water or wind grinds down rock.

clue.text: Loony children's game going around

indicators.note: going around means turning back on itself, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: tig is the British name for the chasing game tag

explanation.surface: A crazy playground game goes round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: A git is British slang for a foolish or unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal insults for a foolish person, used here as nouns.

clue.text: Profoundly dull family extremely upset to relocate

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme ends of a word, its first and last letters
relocating moves the letters to new places, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: first and last letters
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A family is extremely unhappy about having to move house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'to relocate' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To stupefy is to dull the senses or mind completely, as a drug or shock does.

clue.text: Books young 50's trendy carries or carried

indicators.note: a word that carries another holds it inside itself

blocks.note: a Teddy boy, a fashionable British youth of the 1950s
the Old Testament books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fashionable young man of the fifties hauls books around, then or now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carries or carried' looks like a single definition offering two tenses; 'carries' is the container signal and 'carried' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something heavy, so the past form means carried.

clue.text: Compliant matron at heart fit for playing?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

blocks.note: the two central letters
a part that can be acted is actable

explanation.surface: A hospital matron is easy-going at heart, perhaps suited to a stage role.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable means easily managed or docile, which is to be compliant.
